//: Bun OS apps that can stand in for a Windows counterpart, with the gate each must pass before `bunos windows replace <app> on` switches the default, and the reversible switch it uses (docs/WINDOWS-ARCHITECTURE.md, section 'Replacement path'). Switches only change defaults (associations, shell verbs, Windows Terminal profile); no Windows file is deleted, renamed or patched, and every switch is off by default.

files.title: COSMIC Files instead of Explorer windows
files.windows: explorer.exe (folder windows; the shell itself is never replaced)
parity: drag and drop with other apps

terminal.title: nushell as the Windows Terminal default profile (cmd and PowerShell stay installed)
terminal.windows: cmd.exe / powershell.exe as the default WT profile
parity: win <tool> covers services, registry, WMI, COM, events

switch.reason: Rio has no ITerminalHandoff server yet: Windows can only delegate the console to a terminal implementing the OpenConsole handoff COM interfaces (docs/WINDOWS-SHELL.md).

userland.title: uutils/brush userland on PATH
userland.windows: System32 tools of the same name (find, sort, more, ...)

switch.reason: Ordered PATH only: the userland is reached by its own directory on PATH and the nu/brush shells; System32 tools are never shadowed or replaced, so scripts that call find.exe or sort.exe keep Windows' behaviour.

parity: GNU option compatibility for every shipped tool
no System32 name collisions on PATH

window-management.title: Window management
window-management.windows: Snap layouts, Snap groups, virtual desktops

switch.reason: Windows' own window management is the pick; `bunos-win11 apply --module look` turns on and themes it. GlazeWM, tacky-borders and AltSnap are retired (no resident processes).
The taskbar stays; the catalog's shell module declutters it (Widgets, Task View, Chat, search box) by policy.
Start search stays; the catalog turns off web results and suggestions. Flow Launcher is retired.

tweaks.title: Bun OS Tweaks next to Settings

switch.reason: A complement, not a replacement: it writes the same values Settings writes, with a journal and undo.
